 THIS WRIT PETITION IS FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 AND 227 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA PRAYING TO ISSUE WRIT IN THE NATURE OF MANDAMUS BY DIRECTING THE 5TH RESPONDENT TO CONSIDER THE REQUEST OF THE PETITIONER FOR FORWARDED BY THE 3RD RESPONDENT EITHER TO SHIFT THE ROAD OR TO PAY THE COMPENSATION BY ACQUIRING 20 GUNTAS OF LAND OF THE PETITIONER PURSUANT TO PROPOSAL DATED 29.01.2024 VIDE ANNEXURE-G AND COMMUNICATION DATED 21.03.2024 ISSUED BY 4TH RESPONDENT VIDE ANNEXURE-K BY ALLOWING THE WRIT PETITION IN THE ENDS OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY AND ETC.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING,

2  ORAL ORDER (PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE PRADEEP SINGH YERUR)
1. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner.
2. Learned AGA is director take notice for respondent Nos.1 to 5.
3. Petitioner along with his wife and two sons are absolute owners in possession and enjoyment of the land bearing R.S.No.180/1 measuring 5 acres 15 guntas and R.S.No.162/2 measuring 5 acres 1 gunta situated at Hullambi village, Dummavad Hobli in Kalaghatagi taluk of Dharwad district and having purchased the properties by virtue of a registered sale deed, petitioner is in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the above said lands.
4.

In the year 2022, petitioner gave an application to the Assistant Director of Land Records,
Kalaghatagi for subdivision of the lands and acting on the said application, the ADLR conducted survey, prepared PT sheet by issuing notice to the petitioner as well as the neighbours of the NC:
2024:KHC-D:17973 adjacent lands.

According to the petitioner, as per the PT sheet prepared, by the ADLR, shows formation of road by the PWD in the land of petitioner measuring 20 guntas, out of 5 acres 15 guntas, which is without any process of acquisition or notice.
Hence, he contends it is illegal and respondents having not paid any compensation are trying to acquire the property.
According to the petitioner, the respondents are trying to form a road in the land belonging to the petitioner to an extent of 20 guntas.
Therefore petitioner made a representation to either shift the road proposed to be formed, which may fall within the area belonging to the petitioner in his land.

Despite the communication made to the 3rd respondent and the 4th respondent, no action was taken and ultimately the impugned communication was sent to the petitioner vide Annexure-K by the 4th respondent to the petitioner.

Hence petitioner aggrieved by the issuance of Annexure-K, is before this Court seeking a writ of mandamus for a direction to the 5th respondent to consider the request of the petitioner forwarded by the 3rd respondent either to NC: 2024:KHC-D:17973 shift the road being formed in the land of the petitioner or to acquire 20 guntas of land, if it is falling within the land of the petitioner for formation of the road.

5. Learned AGA representing the State contends that Annexure-K is a communication made by the 4th respondent-Assistant Executive Engineer to the petitioner for podi of the property of the petitioner bearing Survey No.180/*/* now bearing Survey No.180/1 to an extent of 20 guntas.
It is not specified in Annexure-K as to whether 20 guntas of land for formation of road, is falling within the land of the petitioner.

What is ordered is for the petitioner to participate for podi of the land and if it is later realized by the respondents that the road that is intended to be formed, falls within the land of the petitioner, then necessary process would be initiated for either acquiring or granting compensation to the petitioner.

If no such process happens of the road, falling within the land of petitioner, the question of granting any compensation or acquisition of the petitioner's land would Sri Manohar Muttappa Nayak vs The State Of Karnataka on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93511298/
3 not arise.

sentences.text: Under the circumstances, learned AGA contends that the process of podi would decide as to what would be the next course of action.
Therefore, he contends that the petition is premature and cannot be considered.
7. Be that as it may, since Annexure-K is issued by the respondent No.4, the petitioner shall participate in the podi of the land for formation of the road.

If the road falls within the land of the petitioner, the next course of action would be for the respondents to either acquire the land or pay compensation to the petitioner for utilising the land of the petitioner.
8. If no such thing of use of road in the land of the petitioner happens, the question of paying compensation or acquisition of the land of petitioner would not arise.

9. Under the circumstances, I pass the following:
ORDER i. Petition is disposed of.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:17973 ii. Petitioner shall participate in the podi of the land for formation of road.

iii. It is made clear that if the road intended to be formed by the respondents, falls within the land of the petitioner, necessary procedure shall be followed by the respondents for acquisition or payment of compensation, in accordance with law.

Sd/-
